candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: apply infection-control principles to invasive devices, recognize healthcare-associated infection risks, and implement measures that reduce bloodstream-infection risk.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — infection risk of hemodialysis vascular-access types
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize central venous dialysis catheters as the hemodialysis access type with the highest bloodstream-infection risk and understand why strict infection-prevention practices are required.

options.A: Central venous catheters have the highest bloodstream-infection risk among the common hemodialysis access types, so meticulous catheter-access and infection-prevention practices are essential.
options.B: Dialysis catheters have a lower infection risk than mature AV fistulas, so special catheter precautions are mainly optional.
options.C: Infection risk is essentially identical for fistulas, grafts, and central venous catheters, regardless of access type.
options.D: Catheter-related bloodstream infection is usually minor and does not justify ongoing access-care precautions after insertion.

candidate.rationale: CDC identifies vascular-access type as a major risk factor for bloodstream infection in people receiving hemodialysis. AV fistulas have the lowest infection risk, AV grafts have an intermediate risk, and central venous catheters have the highest infection risk. CDC therefore emphasizes catheter reduction and meticulous catheter-access care, hub disinfection, aseptic technique, and patient education as core bloodstream-infection prevention strategies. A is correct; B reverses the risk hierarchy, C ignores established differences among access types, and D minimizes a potentially serious complication.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly supports the dialysis-access infection-risk hierarchy and the heightened importance of bloodstream-infection prevention for central venous dialysis catheters.
candidate.source_document_title: Infections and Patients on Dialysis; Best Practices for Bloodstream Infection Prevention in the Dialysis Setting
